blocks.text: In AC circuits the opposition to the current is called impedance, Z. It includes both resistance R, the opposition due to resistors, and reactance X, the opposition due to capacitors (capacitive reactance XC) and inductors (inductive reactance XL). A purely resistive circuit has only resistance and no reactance.

blocks.title: Impedance
blocks.text: Impedance is the combined effect of resistance and reactances in an AC circuit. It is the ratio of the rms voltage to the rms current: Z = Vrms / Irms (17.20). Its SI unit is the ohm.
Because the voltages across R, L and C are not in phase, resistance and reactance cannot simply be added. They are added as vectors (phasors), as the next sections show.

An AC circuit has a peak voltage of 200 V and a peak current of 10 A. Find its impedance. Solution: Vrms = 0.707 x 200 V = 141.4 V and Irms = 0.707 x 10 A = 7.07 A, so Z = Vrms / Irms = 141.4 V / 7.07 A = 20 ohm. (The same result follows from Vo/Io = 200/10.)

blocks.prompt: Why can the resistance and reactance of a circuit not simply be added to find its impedance?
blocks.explanation: Because the voltages across a resistor and a reactance are 90 degrees out of phase; they must be added as vectors (by Pythagoras for R and X).

items: Impedance Z = Vrms / Irms: total opposition (R and X) in ohms.
R and X add as vectors, not as numbers.
